note: Source manifest for the ORCH-753 gold cohort. The paper text is NOT committed; it lives at C:/t/eval-fulltext/<PMCID>.txt and gold.load_fulltext refuses a text whose sha256 differs.
citation: Meng Q et al. Itaconate transport across the plasma membrane and Salmonella-containing vacuole via MCT1/4 modulates macrophage antibacterial activity Nature communications 2025.
pathway_in_one_line: Macrophages make itaconate from cis-aconitate and then export it through MCT1 and MCT4, both across the plasma membrane and, with RAB32, into the Salmonella-containing vacuole, so blocking the transporters raises intracellular itaconate and kills more bacteria.
scope_note: In scope: the one named conversion cis-aconitate -> itaconate by IRG1/ACOD1 (decarboxylation), itaconate export across the plasma membrane by MCT1 and MCT4, itaconate delivery into the Salmonella-containing vacuole by MCT1/MCT4 with RAB32, and the consequence chain where loss of that export raises intracellular itaconate and suppresses Salmonella replication. Adjacent: the TCA-cycle break at IDH1 that raises cis-aconitate (stated as an increase, not as a named conversion), itaconate inhibition of bacterial targets, and all pharmacology (AZD3965, VB124, Su3118, IRG1-IN-1) and knockout phenotyping. A drafter must not turn an inhibitor into a pathway participant.
selected_because: The transport row needs a eukaryotic case, and this one has what the Dpp structure paper lacks: a named small-molecule cargo, two distinct membranes crossed in the same pathway, a named accessory factor for one of them, and one real chemical step feeding the transported pool. It is also host-pathogen, so it mixes two organisms in one pathway - a case the current gold never tests and one where organism tagging can fail silently.
